$comment: Every number here is a floor somebody raised deliberately. Lowering one needs a commit message that says why. The `hard` entries are not per-case negotiable: they are the claims the product makes.
$catalog: The ratchet. `checkCatalog` validates a rule's SHAPE — docs present, reason present — and never its REACHABILITY, so a rule can be well-formed, cited, and unable to fire in any repository. The runner fails when a rule outside the allowlist goes unexercised (a new dead rule), and fails when a listed one starts firing (the list is stale). It may only shrink.

$neverExercisedWhy.cargo.package.description: A `pointer` matcher on `**/Cargo.toml`. There is no TOML extractor, so the file falls to the residual sweep and `classify` short-circuits on `tier === 'sweep'` before `matchRules` is called. Remedy: src/extract/toml.ts.
$neverExercisedWhy.python.pyproject.description: Same file format, same missing extractor.
$neverExercisedWhy.docker.label: A `keyName` matcher on `**/Dockerfile*`. Dockerfile is read by the prose extractor, whose sites carry `key = "p[0]"`, so the pattern never matches. Remedy: a Dockerfile extractor that emits LABEL keys, or a rule that matches the value instead.
$neverExercisedWhy.html.title: Matches `{kind: attr, element: title, attr: text}`, but the HTML extractor emits a document title as a `prose-run` at `title/text[0]`. The title IS found and translated — by the generic prose path — so this is a traceability gap, not a recall one.
